# Potential gains and brain activity

Does increasing potential monetary gain produce a greater fMRI response in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) in the NARPS equal-indifference group?

Test the hypothesis that this response increases with potential gain.
Participants performed a mixed-gambles task, deciding whether to accept gambles with possible gains and losses.
In this group, the range of potential gains was twice the range of potential losses.

Investigate the question at the group-analysis stage using the supplied 54 participant gain-effect maps and metadata.
Preprocessing and individual modeling are fixed inputs, described in `upstream-methods.md`; do not repeat them or download time-series scans.
Choose scientifically defensible group models, quality checks, software and visualizations.
Account for what the supplied effect estimates measure and the limits of their upstream model.
Use whole-brain correction for multiple comparisons when evaluating support for the hypothesis, as required by the original study; justify how you identify vmPFC.

Produce a concise scientific report with informative figures and the code and results supporting your conclusions.
Explain uncertainty, exclusions and limitations, including what a lack of support would mean.
Prior teams' answers are not ground truth or a required result.

Source: [NARPS original analysis instructions, Hypothesis 1](https://www.narps.info/files/narps_instructions_for_analysis_teams.pdf).

Common execution resources

Use the root Pixi environment; add dependencies as needed. Keep analysis outputs under `results/` in this experiment repository. For substantive analyses, capture complete command metadata, stdout/stderr, resource usage and run summaries with duct under `logs/`. Retain failed attempts and annex large outputs/logs.
Keep task-specific installations local to this experiment repository; do not change shared user configuration.

Use the supplied, pinned STAMPED skills to complete this study: start with do-full-research-loop and apply the related guidance where appropriate.
I’ll follow the supplied STAMPED research loop, first checking its pinned workflow and the experiment’s inputs, then carrying out and documenting the group analysis.

content.text: The protocol will test a positive population mean of participant gain-effect estimates voxelwise with a one-sided, whole-brain max-statistic permutation test. That fits the supplied cope maps better than treating them as t/z maps; absent participant variance maps mean a conventional first-level variance-weighted mixed-effects analysis cannot be reconstructed. I’ll use the corrected whole-brain result as the hypothesis test and report vmPFC localization anatomically, without selecting a region from the observed map.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: analysis-protocol.md
+# Analysis protocol: NARPS Hypothesis 1, equal-indifference group
+
+## Question and scope
+
+Test whether the population mean gain-effect estimate is positive in any vmPFC voxel in the 54-member equal-indifference group, at the group-analysis stage. The fixed inputs are the 54 AO86 participant cope maps, metadata and upstream methods in `input/`; no time-series scans or upstream reanalysis are in scope.
+
+## Data and estimand
+
+- Unit: participant; one unthresholded participant-level gain contrast parameter estimate map per participant, averaged across four runs upstream.
+- Population: all 54 participants in the supplied equalIndifference cohort. Join map IDs to `input/participants.tsv`; duplicate, missing, nonfinite, geometry-mismatched and all-zero maps are checked. Exclude no participant based on observed effect magnitude. If a map fails a prespecified integrity check, report it and stop rather than silently changing the sample.
+- Target: mean of participant cope estimates at each voxel, and its one-sided group statistic. These cope values use a mean-centered, variance-normalized gain modulator upstream; they are not per-currency-unit slopes, standardized statistics, nor raw BOLD change. Gain is modeled separately from loss, so the estimate is conditional on that first-level model.
+- Group inference: one-sample positive one-sided t statistic with equal participant weights; sign-flip permutation under a symmetric zero-centered null, with max statistic across all in-mask voxels for whole-brain family-wise error control. Use 9,999 random permutations, fixed seed, add-one p-values, alpha=.05. Report effect estimates and uncertainty as well as the corrected inference.
+- Search mask: intersection of finite, nonzero support across all 54 maps, with identical dimensions and affine required. This uses the supplied maps only and defines the spatial family before testing. Document mask voxel count and volume. A predefined vmPFC anatomical overlay (Harvard-Oxford cortical atlas: Frontal Medial Cortex and Subcallosal Cortex labels) will identify localization; it does not narrow the correction family or determine support.
+
+## Quality checks and uncertainty
+
+Verify exact cohort-to-map correspondence, file checksums against `input/sources.json`, NIfTI dimensions/affines/spatial reference, finite values, nonzero support and per-map summary distributions. Inspect group mean and subject-level vmPFC ROI distribution. Use a participant bootstrap interval for the descriptive vmPFC ROI mean if implemented; whole-brain significance remains based on the max-statistic permutation test. Variance maps and the full first-level pipeline are absent, so inverse-variance mixed-effects inference cannot be reconstructed. The cope-only group model relies on exchangeability/symmetry and may be less efficient or less calibrated than a model using participant variances.
+
+## Interpretation and stopping rules
+
+Hypothesis support requires at least one positive whole-brain FWE-corrected voxel anatomically within the predefined vmPFC overlay. Report all corrected whole-brain findings; do not select among models by significance. No corrected vmPFC result is lack of evidence at this sample size and analysis resolution, not evidence of no effect. State whether correction was based on the full in-mask family and whether any exclusions occurred. Retain command/log metadata and output summaries under `logs/`; scientific outputs and figures go under `results/`.
*** End Patch";

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: scripts/analyze.py
+#!/usr/bin/env python
+"""Group analysis of supplied NARPS AO86 gain cope maps."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import nibabel as nib
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+from nilearn import datasets, plotting, image
+from scipy import stats
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+INPUT = ROOT / "input"
+OUT = ROOT / "results"
+SEED = 20261015
+N_PERM = 9999
+
+
+def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as stream:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
+            h.update(chunk)
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+
+def read_maps():
+    participants = pd.read_csv(INPUT / "participants.tsv", sep="\t")
+    sources = json.loads((INPUT / "sources.json").read_text())
+    if len(participants) != 54 or participants.participant_id.duplicated().any():
+        raise ValueError("Expected 54 unique cohort rows")
+    expected_ids = {v["participant_id"] for k, v in sources["files"].items()
+                    if k.endswith("_cope.nii.gz")}
+    if set(participants.participant_id) != expected_ids or len(expected_ids) != 54:
+        raise ValueError("Participant metadata and source map IDs do not match exactly")
+    paths = [INPUT / "data" / f"{pid}_hypo1_cope.nii.gz"
+             for pid in participants.participant_id]
+    images = [nib.load(str(path)) for path in paths]
+    ref = images[0]
+    shape, affine = ref.shape, ref.affine
+    arrays = []
+    file_qc = []
+    for pid, path, img in zip(participants.participant_id, paths, images):
+        if img.shape != shape or not np.allclose(img.affine, affine, atol=1e-5):
+            raise ValueError(f"Spatial geometry mismatch for {pid}")
+        x = img.get_fdata(dtype=np.float32)
+        finite = np.isfinite(x)
+        if not finite.all():
+            raise ValueError(f"Nonfinite voxel values in {pid}")
+        if not np.any(x != 0):
+            raise ValueError(f"All-zero image for {pid}")
+        arrays.append(x)
+        file_qc.append({"participant_id": pid, "sha256": sha256(path),
+                        "shape": list(shape), "finite_voxels": int(finite.sum()),
+                        "nonzero_voxels": int(np.count_nonzero(x)),
+                        "mean_nonzero": float(x[x != 0].mean()),
+                        "sd_nonzero": float(x[x != 0].std(ddof=1))})
+    return participants, sources, paths, images, np.stack(arrays), file_qc
+
+
+def save_json(obj, path: Path):
+    path.write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+
+
+def vmPFC_atlas_mask(reference):
+    atlas = datasets.fetch_atlas_harvard_oxford("cort-maxprob-thr25-2mm")
+    atlas_img = nib.load(atlas.maps)
+    labels = list(atlas.labels)
+    wanted = {"Frontal Medial Cortex", "Subcallosal Cortex"}
+    absent = wanted.difference(labels)
+    if absent:
+        raise ValueError(f"Atlas is missing predefined vmPFC labels: {sorted(absent)}")
+    resampled = image.resample_to_img(atlas_img, reference, interpolation="nearest")
+    atlas_values = resampled.get_fdata().astype(int)
+    ids = [labels.index(label) for label in wanted]
+    mask = np.isin(atlas_values, ids)
+    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    atlas_copy = OUT / "harvard_oxford_cort_maxprob_thr25_2mm.nii.gz"
+    if not atlas_copy.exists():
+        nib.save(atlas_img, str(atlas_copy))
+    return mask, sorted(wanted), labels, atlas_copy
+
+
+def group_test(arrays, reference, n_perm=N_PERM, seed=SEED):
+    # The shared nonzero support is the whole-brain family. The atlas does not
+    # restrict this family and cannot affect the corrected p values.
+    mask = np.isfinite(arrays).all(axis=0) & np.all(arrays != 0, axis=0)
+    n = arrays.shape[0]
+    y = arrays[:, mask].astype(np.float64, copy=False)
+    if y.shape[1] < 1000:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unexpectedly small common whole-brain mask: {y.shape[1]}")
+    sum_y = y.sum(axis=0)
+    sumsq = np.square(y).sum(axis=0)
+    denom = np.sqrt(np.maximum(n * sumsq - sum_y * sum_y, 0.0))
+    observed = sum_y * np.sqrt(n - 1) / denom
+    observed[denom == 0] = 0.0
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+    max_null = np.empty(n_perm, dtype=np.float64)
+    # Sign flips are at the independent participant level. Batch matrix
+    # multiplication bounds memory use while evaluating every in-mask voxel.
+    batch_size = 32
+    for start in range(0, n_perm, batch_size):
+        stop = min(start + batch_size, n_perm)
+        signs = rng.choice(np.array([-1.0, 1.0]), size=(stop - start, n))
+        sums = signs @ y
+        perm_denom = np.sqrt(np.maximum(n * sumsq[None, :] - sums * sums, 0.0))
+        t_perm = sums * np.sqrt(n - 1) / perm_denom
+        t_perm[perm_denom == 0] = 0.0
+        max_null[start:stop] = t_perm.max(axis=1)
+    fwe = (1 + (max_null[:, None] >= observed[None, :]).sum(axis=0)) / (n_perm + 1)
+    mean = np.zeros(mask.shape, dtype=np.float32)
+    tmap = np.zeros(mask.shape, dtype=np.float32)
+    pmap = np.ones(mask.shape, dtype=np.float32)
+    mean[mask] = y.mean(axis=0).astype(np.float32)
+    tmap[mask] = observed.astype(np.float32)
+    pmap[mask] = fwe.astype(np.float32)
+    return mask, mean, tmap, pmap, max_null, observed
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--pilot", action="store_true", help="integrity/QC pilot only")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    participants, sources, paths, imgs, arrays, file_qc = read_maps()
+    mask = np.isfinite(arrays).all(axis=0) & np.all(arrays != 0, axis=0)
+    if args.pilot:
+        pilot = {"n_participants": len(participants), "participants": participants.participant_id.tolist(),
+                 "shape": list(arrays.shape[1:]), "affine": imgs[0].affine.tolist(),
+                 "common_nonzero_mask_voxels": int(mask.sum()),
+                 "common_mask_volume_mm3": float(mask.sum() * abs(np.linalg.det(imgs[0].affine[:3, :3]))),
+                 "map_qc": file_qc}
+        save_json(pilot, OUT / "pilot-qc.json")
+        print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in pilot.items() if k != "map_qc"}, indent=2))
+        return
+
+    roi_mask, roi_labels, atlas_labels, atlas_path = vmPFC_atlas_mask(imgs[0])
+    mask, mean, tmap, pmap, max_null, observed = group_test(arrays, imgs[0])
+    voxel_volume = abs(np.linalg.det(imgs[0].affine[:3, :3]))
+    n = len(participants)
+    roi = roi_mask & mask
+    if not roi.any():
+        raise ValueError("Predefined vmPFC ROI has no voxels in the group mask")
+    roi_values = arrays[:, roi].mean(axis=1)
+    roi_mean = float(roi_values.mean())
+    roi_sem = float(stats.sem(roi_values))
+    roi_ci = stats.t.interval(0.95, df=n - 1, loc=roi_mean, scale=roi_sem)
+    # Participant bootstrap is a descriptive uncertainty check for the ROI mean.
+    boot_rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED + 1)
+    boot_idx = boot_rng.integers(0, n, size=(20000, n))
+    boot_means = roi_values[boot_idx].mean(axis=1)
+    boot_ci = np.quantile(boot_means, [0.025, 0.975]).tolist()
+    brain_sig = (pmap <= 0.05) & mask & (tmap > 0)
+    roi_sig = brain_sig & roi_mask
+    affine = imgs[0].affine
+    def save_map(data, name):
+        nib.save(nib.Nifti1Image(data, affine, imgs[0].header), str(OUT / name))
+    save_map(mean, "group-mean.nii.gz")
+    save_map(tmap, "group-t-positive.nii.gz")
+    save_map(pmap, "group-fwe-p-positive.nii.gz")
+    save_map(mask.astype(np.uint8), "whole-brain-mask.nii.gz")
+    save_map(roi_mask.astype(np.uint8), "vmPFC-atlas-mask.nii.gz")
+    peak = None
+    if brain_sig.any():
+        coords = np.argwhere(brain_sig)
+        peak_idx = tuple(coords[np.argmax(tmap[brain_sig])])
+        peak = {"ijk": list(peak_idx), "mni_mm": nib.affines.apply_affine(affine, peak_idx).tolist(),
+                "t": float(tmap[peak_idx]), "fwe_p": float(pmap[peak_idx]),
+                "in_predefined_vmPFC": bool(roi_mask[peak_idx])}
+    # ROI peak summary and whole-brain result are distinct outputs.
+    roi_t = tmap[roi]
+    roi_p = pmap[roi]
+    roi_peak_flat = int(np.argmax(roi_t))
+    roi_idx = tuple(np.argwhere(roi)[roi_peak_flat])
+    summary = {
+        "analysis": "one-sample positive t; participant sign-flips; max-t whole-brain FWE",
+        "n_participants": n, "n_excluded": 0, "permutations": N_PERM, "seed": SEED,
+        "alpha": 0.05, "one_sided": True,
+        "shape": list(mask.shape), "voxel_volume_mm3": voxel_volume,
+        "whole_brain_mask_voxels": int(mask.sum()), "whole_brain_mask_volume_mm3": float(mask.sum() * voxel_volume),
+        "vmPFC_definition": "Harvard-Oxford cortical max-probability atlas threshold 25%; union of Frontal Medial Cortex and Subcallosal Cortex",
+        "vmPFC_atlas_labels": roi_labels, "vmPFC_atlas_sha256": sha256(atlas_path),
+        "vmPFC_intersection_voxels": int(roi.sum()),
+        "vmPFC_mean_across_voxels": roi_mean,
+        "vmPFC_mean_t_CI95": [float(v) for v in roi_ci],
+        "vmPFC_participant_bootstrap_CI95": [float(v) for v in boot_ci],
+        "vmPFC_participant_values": [{"participant_id": pid, "mean_cope": float(v)}
+                                     for pid, v in zip(participants.participant_id, roi_values)],
+        "vmPFC_peak": {"ijk": list(roi_idx), "mni_mm": nib.affines.apply_affine(affine, roi_idx).tolist(),
+                       "t": float(tmap[roi_idx]), "fwe_p": float(pmap[roi_idx])},
+        "n_whole_brain_fwe_voxels": int(brain_sig.sum()),
+        "n_vmPFC_fwe_voxels": int(roi_sig.sum()), "global_positive_peak": peak,
+        "max_null_t_95pct": float(np.quantile(max_null, .95)),
+        "max_null_t_99pct": float(np.quantile(max_null, .99)),
+        "map_qc": file_qc,
+        "notes": ["Effect estimates are not currency-unit slopes or standardized test statistics.",
+                  "No participant-level variance maps are supplied; equal-weight cope model used.",
+                  "Common nonzero support defines the whole-brain family."]
+    }
+    save_json(summary, OUT / "results.json")
+    pd.DataFrame({"participant_id": participants.participant_id, "mean_vmPFC_cope": roi_values}).to_csv(
+        OUT / "vmPFC-participant-values.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
+
+    # Atlas surface/volumetric visualization: corrected t map over the
+    # predeclared vmPFC anatomical mask; include unthresholded mean separately.
+    sig_img = nib.Nifti1Image(np.where(brain_sig & roi_mask, tmap, 0).astype(np.float32), affine, imgs[0].header)
+    display = plotting.plot_stat_map(sig_img, bg_img=None, display_mode="z",
+                                     cut_coords=[-20, -10, 0, 10, 20],
+                                     title="Positive group effect in predefined vmPFC\n(whole-brain max-T FWE p ≤ .05)",
+                                     threshold=0.01, cmap="cold_hot", colorbar=True,
+                                     output_file=str(OUT / "vmPFC-corrected-slices.png"))
+    plotting.close()
+    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.2), constrained_layout=True)
+    jitter = np.random.default_rng(SEED).normal(0, 0.045, size=n)
+    ax.scatter(jitter, roi_values, s=26, alpha=.72, color="#345995", edgecolor="white", linewidth=.4)
+    ax.axhline(0, color="#555555", linewidth=1, linestyle="--")
+    ax.errorbar([0], [roi_mean], yerr=[[roi_mean - roi_ci[0]], [roi_ci[1] - roi_mean]],
+                fmt="D", color="#c0392b", markersize=7, capsize=5, label="Mean and t-based 95% CI")
+    ax.set(xlim=(-.35, .35), xticks=[], ylabel="Mean participant cope in vmPFC atlas ROI",
+           title="Participant variation in predefined vmPFC ROI")
+    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="best")
+    fig.savefig(OUT / "vmPFC-participant-distribution.png", dpi=180)
+    plt.close(fig)
+    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in summary.items() if k not in {"map_qc", "vmPFC_participant_values"}}, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
*** End Patch";
const r = await tools.apply_patch(patch);
text(r);
